newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour holds 21-point lead in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour holds 21-point lead in latest poll.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party has held on to its 21-point lead over the Conservatives, even though support for both parties has dipped by two points, an opinion poll published on Thursday showed.

The MORI poll for the Times newspaper put support for Labour at 50 percent while the Conservatives were at 29 percent. The same poll a month ago put Labour at 52 percent and the Conservatives at 31 percent.

The main beneficiary was the Liberal Democrat party which gained three points to 14 percent, but billionaire Sir James Goldsmith's Referendum Party also scored its best poll rating to date, with three percent.

Labour held on to its lead despite the fact that a majority of voters disbelieve its vows not to raise taxes. The MORI poll showed two thirds thought a Labour government would increase income tax while more than half said it would not improve their standard of living.
The poll also showed that around a quarter of voters thought they may change their mind about who they will vote for before polling day on May 1.
